rationale: 89 items (41+13+35). Balance lane in the 88-90 window that every lane must occupy: the 892-item run over ten lanes forces a maximum of at least 90, and the 88-item batch 25 forces a minimum of at most 88. Keeps the 20->14 dependency (6 edges) internal and mixes algebraic-geometry (1, 20) with scheme-theory (14); the window admits only one same-category triple in the whole run, (13,23,24), so lanes like this must mix categories.

label: b

label: c

Mixes representation-theory (3) with algebraic-geometry (22) and braid-groups (9).

label: d

label: e

label: f

label: h
rationale: 89 items (17+19+53). Grouping 23 with 24 instead would use the window's single same-category triple (13/23/24) but raise crossings to 109, so the edge-minimal 108 is preferred.

label: i
rationale: 89 items (69+20). Batch 27 (69) cannot enter any triple of the window (69+13+13 = 95 > 90), so it takes the run's only two-batch lane; partner 24 (20 items) keeps the lane at 89 and reaches the minimum 108 crossing edges, better than the 109 that any 19-item partner (9, 10 or 17) gives. The pair mixes algebraic-geometry (27) with scheme-theory (24), as every non-singleton lane must.

label: j
rationale: 88 items, batch 25 alone. Indivisible at this balance: its smallest possible partner (13) gives 101 and breaks the 90 ceiling, so it is a forced singleton lane, and its 88 caps the partition minimum at 88. Hence the best possible maximum (90 = ceil(892/10)) and spread (2) are both attained; Step 2 cannot balance this batch further, and the limit is reported rather than hidden.
